Subject: Question on intermediary fees and currency for INV-2026-089

Hi Soojin,

We're preparing payment for invoice INV-2026-089. A couple of specifics before we schedule the transfer:

- Our bank defaults to SHA and has historically deducted intermediary correspondent charges; we want to avoid short-pays. If we request OUR, they need a written confirmation from Redwood stating that any subsequent deductions will not be re-billed to us. Can you provide a short statement we can paste into their instruction?

- The invoice lists USD amounts. We prefer to pay in EUR from our euro treasury. Do you accept EUR and, if so, how do you handle VAT and the FX conversion on your side? Do you require us to include any particular rate or reference?

- Finally, please confirm beneficiary bank details (IBAN/SWIFT) for both USD (US correspondent) and EUR (SEPA) rails so we can populate their transfer screen.

Attaching a screenshot of our bank's payment UI which shows the charge type dropdown.

Thanks,
Marta Delgado
Head of Finance Operations
GlobalApps Inc.

Attachment: payment_form_screenshot.png (image stub)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Delgado <finance@globalapps.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-22T11:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on intermediary fees and currency for INV-2026-089

Hi Marta,

Thanks for the clear note. Short answers first: we can accept EUR, but to guarantee Redwood receives the full USD-equivalent invoice amount you should instruct YOUR bank to send with OUR charges. If you must use SHA, we will detect short pays and either post a recovery invoice or absorb small amounts per our threshold (see below).

Full details:
- Preferred currency: USD. If you pay USD, the landed amount on our ledger is deterministic. If you pay EUR we accept it and our FX desk will convert on settlement; the converted USD we record will be the bank settlement rate for the value date. If you need an indicative USD amount ahead of settlement, request an "indicative conversion" and we can provide one but it is not final.

- VAT: Redwood Inference is a UK/EMEA vendor for this invoice. If GlobalApps is VAT-registered in the EU and supplies a valid VAT number we will apply reverse charge (no VAT on Redwood invoice). Please include your VAT number on the payment reference or attach it to the payment remittance so our AR team can match. If no VAT number is provided, local VAT rules may apply and we will follow up.

- Charges: OUR = originator pays all charges (preferred). SHA = shared (likely deductions by correspondents). BEN = beneficiary pays (not recommended).

Bank details (copy/paste rows for your treasury):

I've attached a small text file with these rows for copy/paste.

Operational note: if your payment uses SHA and our received USD is short, our billing team will create a short-pay recovery invoice for any net deficit >= $20 USD. Amounts under $20 are absorbed as operational variance. If you'd like us to raise recovery invoices for any shortfall regardless of size, say so and we will change the threshold for this customer.

I'll Cc our AR lead Laura for VAT confirmation and Ben for any correspondent bank caveats.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Hi Marta,

Quick VAT/process confirmation from Revenue Ops:
- If GlobalApps provides a valid EU VAT number, Redwood will treat the invoice under reverse charge (no VAT collected). Please include the VAT number in the payment reference or email it to AR@redwood.ai.
- For EUR receipts we post the converted USD at the bank settlement FX rate for the value date. We can provide an indicative USD amount upon request but final posting will use settled funds.
- Short-pay threshold: as Soojin noted we auto-issue recovery invoices for shortfalls >= $20 USD. We can set a lower threshold for strategic accounts; tell me if GlobalApps wants that.

Laura Bennett
Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

"Please execute payment with OUR charges so that Redwood Inference receives the full invoiced amount. Any charges applied by intermediary or correspondent banks should be borne by the originator. Reference INV-2026-089 / GlobalApps."

If intermediaries still deduct despite OUR marked, please notify AR@redwood.ai and we will investigate on a case-by-case basis.
